A1.justification: Both PDFs describe XHugWBC and contain complete main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original simulation and real-robot experiments, including tracking errors, survival rates, fine-tuning results, architecture ablations, and loco-manipulation demonstrations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4.1–4.6 and the appendices, including Tables 1, 2, and 7 and Figures 3–9.

M1.justification: The randomization procedure, canonical joint mapping, policy architectures, state estimator, and rewards remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 corrects the explanation of masked versus unmasked attention; the layer order and equations already specified the same architecture in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same twelve simulated humanoid types, seven real-world robot configurations, procedural training domain, and locomotion/teleoperation tasks. Figure 8's changed robot labels do not establish changed evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: HugWBC specialists, MetaMorph, MorAL, and Naive Random remain in their corresponding comparisons in Tables 1 and 7 and Figures 3 and 5. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Table 3 revises reported randomization settings: shear ranges change from mostly [0.9, 1.1] to [-0.1, 0.1], translations become centered offsets scaled by reference link lengths, and scaling rows change from d_i to exp(d_i). Table 5 changes Booster K1's mass from 20 to 18 kg. These are localized setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The architecture ablation, latent-representation analysis, fine-tuning analyses, and real-world case studies are retained. Corresponding plots and demonstration images contain no new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repeated trials averaged for the sim-to-real evaluation and retain the same uncertainty-reporting format. One uncertainty value changes in Table 7, but no statistical procedure, run count, or seed information changes.

E6.justification: Table 7 changes Fourier N1's Generalist-FT angular-velocity tracking error from 0.135 (±0.890) to 0.135 (±0.089) rad/s. The mean is unchanged, and the remaining numerical results and plotted findings match.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.3 corrects the affine-transformation statement from x' = E x to homogeneous coordinates q' = E q, resolving a dimensional inconsistency with the pseudo-inertia expression. Section 3.1 also corrects the first mass moment from m c^T to m c. The propositions and Appendix A.1 derivation otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The claims of broad zero-shot transfer, approximately 85% of specialist return, and up to 10% improvement after fine-tuning remain. Removing one introductory first-time phrase does not remove the retained novelty claim in the contribution list.

C2.justification: The new Impact Statement explicitly acknowledges that randomization requires embodiment-specific parameter ranges. Section 4.5 refines its hardware explanation from larger transmission reducers to larger gear reduction ratios. Existing command-interface and motion-retargeting limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly defines reference link bounding-box lengths in the body frame, clarifying the translation ranges in Table 3. Randomization quantities and Booster K1's reported hardware mass are revised. The remaining reward, architecture, and deployment details are retained.

R1.justification: The separate Pinocchio software reference dated 2015–2021 and its Appendix B.2 citation are removed, while the 2019 Pinocchio paper remains. Other bibliography changes largely update metadata for retained works, including AnyMorph; research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized grammar, terminology, notation, and bibliographic edits, adds acknowledgments and an Impact Statement, and updates contribution and conference front matter. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 correctly relabels the existing percentage measure as Relative Gap, Table 3 is compressed, and appendix tables are rearranged. Figure 2 receives a spelling correction. Figure 8 introduces incorrect Unitree G1 labels for the unchanged Agibot X2 and EngineAI PM01 images.

improvement.justification: V3 improves internal consistency through the relative-gap label, corrected attention explanation, and clearer randomization parameters, while explicitly acknowledging a randomization limitation. These limited clarity and reproducibility gains outweigh the new Figure 8 labeling errors. The unchanged experimental evidence and unexplained setting revisions limit the overall improvement.
